discoveryRequests.query: Available operations for browser automation: open/navigate to URL, search Amazon.fr, observe page, click links/buttons, extract text/HTML/structured product fields, handle pagination or truncated observations, close browser in cleanup.
Available operations for creating and saving an Excel XLSX workbook at a specified disk path with rows/columns for product name, description, price, and explicit missing/CAPTCHA status.

requirements.summary: Accept one public input named query, search Amazon.fr for that article, inspect at most the first 10 products, extract each product’s name, description, and price without inventing missing data, save the results to workflows/schema-portability-20261002/compactbindings20261006b-amazon-1/products.xlsx, and close the browser even on failure.

outcomes.description: Amazon.fr is used to search for the provided query.
At most the first 10 observed product results are processed.
For each processed product, visit its page and extract name, description, and price; CAPTCHA, absent prices, or absent data are recorded explicitly rather than inferred.
An Excel workbook is saved on disk at workflows/schema-portability-20261002/compactbindings20261006b-amazon-1/products.xlsx.
The browser is closed even if the workflow fails.

tasks.objective: Build the Amazon.fr search URL from the single public input query by percent-encoding the query and appending it to https://www.amazon.fr/s?k=. Do not add any other public inputs.
Open the Amazon.fr search results page for the encoded query and capture rendered HTML for later extraction. Use Amazon.fr only.

From the rendered Amazon.fr search page HTML, extract only fields needed before interaction: whether a CAPTCHA/blocker is visible and, if present, the CSS selector of an observed cookie/consent accept button. Do not infer product data here.
If an observed Amazon.fr cookie/consent accept control exists, click it once; otherwise do nothing. This is limited to an observed consent control and does not grant any other authority.
Click the observed cookie/consent accept control so product search results can be read.
Read the current Amazon.fr search page after any consent handling. Capture enough HTML to extract the first observed product-result links and explicit blockers such as CAPTCHA.

Extract, in page order, at most the first 10 observed Amazon.fr product result links from the search results HTML. Also preserve whether the search page shows CAPTCHA/blocking or no observed product links. Return only fields needed for visiting product pages.
For each of the at most 10 extracted Amazon.fr product links, visit the product page and extract per-item details. Preserve order and keep CAPTCHA or absent fields explicit.
Open this product page from the observed search result link and capture rendered HTML for detail extraction.
Read the current product page title region, if present, as text. Empty or absent content remains explicit and is not invented.
Read observed price regions on the current product page, if present, as text. Empty or absent price remains explicit and is not invented.
Read observed product description/bullets regions on the current product page, if present, as text. Empty or absent description remains explicit and is not invented.

For this product visit, produce one product record with name, description, price, and status. Use the specific title/price/description reads first, fall back only to fields explicitly present in the product page HTML, and mark CAPTCHA or missing fields in status instead of inventing values.

Combine the per-product visit results with search-page blocker information. If CAPTCHA blocked the search or no product links were observed, create an explicit status record. Generate TSV rows for an .xlsx workbook with columns name, description, price, status, normalizing embedded tabs/newlines and leaving absent data explicit rather than invented.
Save the extracted Amazon.fr product details to the required Excel workbook path as tab-separated rows converted to .xlsx by the document writer.

always.objective: Close the browser page and context even if any previous search, extraction, or write step fails.

tasks.objective: Build the Amazon.fr search URL from the single public input query by percent-encoding the query and appending it to https://www.amazon.fr/s?k=. Do not add any other public inputs or scenario-specific constants beyond the required Amazon.fr search endpoint.

Open Amazon.fr search results for the encoded query and capture a bounded immutable observation manifest. This manifest is used only to inspect blockers and authorized consent controls before any click.

Consume every page listed in the initial search observation manifest before any navigation or click invalidates its snapshot. Reject incomplete manifests rather than treating partial observations as complete.
Read this frozen initial search observation page by cursor, with no selector, URL, or limit overrides.
Project only the complete observation records needed by later extraction. Reject a truncated page read explicitly.

From the complete initial search observation records, extract only whether an explicit CAPTCHA/blocker is observed and the CSS selector of an actually observed cookie/consent accept control, if any. Do not extract product fields or infer site-specific selectors.
If and only if the complete observation exposed an authorized cookie/consent accept control, click that observed selector once. Otherwise perform no browser action.
Click the observed consent accept control. The selector comes from the complete source observation and grants no other authority.

After any consent handling, capture a fresh bounded immutable observation manifest of the current Amazon.fr search page. This fresh manifest is the authoritative source for product-result links and blockers.
Consume every page listed in the fresh search observation manifest before navigating to any product page. Reject captureTruncated or manifestTruncated instead of assuming page delivery completeness.
Read this frozen fresh search observation page by cursor, with no selector, URL, or limit overrides.
Project only complete observation records needed to extract product-result links and blocker indicators. Reject a truncated page read explicitly.

From the complete fresh search observation records, extract in observed page order at most the first 10 Amazon.fr product-result links, plus observed blocker/no-result indicators. Use only links actually present in the observation; do not invent product URLs, selectors, filtering, sorting, or flattening beyond the bounded first-10 projection.

Sequentially visit each observed product link, at most the 10 links extracted from the complete search manifest. For each product, consume the complete product observation manifest before extracting fields or moving to the next link.
Navigate to this observed product URL and capture a bounded immutable observation manifest for the product page.
Consume every page listed in this product page manifest before any subsequent navigation. Reject incomplete product manifests rather than extracting from partial evidence.
Read this frozen product observation page by cursor, with no selector, URL, or limit overrides.
Project only the complete product observation records needed for field extraction. Reject a truncated product page read explicitly.

From this product's complete observation records, extract only source-grounded business fields: name, description, price, and blocker/missing-field booleans. Use observed values only; nullable fields remain null when absent. Do not create status labels or metadata in this extraction.

Use compact search and product extraction results to create final product records and tab-separated workbook content. Preserve order and completeness. If CAPTCHA, no observed product links, or absent fields are present, record explicit status text rather than inventing data; do not treat missing or incomplete data as an empty successful product list. Normalize embedded tabs and line breaks in TSV cells.
Write the actual Excel workbook to the required relative path. The document writer converts the tab-separated content into .xlsx rows with columns name, description, price, and status.

always.objective: Close the browser page and context unconditionally, even if search, completeness guards, extraction, or workbook writing fails.

Preserve the at-most-10 limit and product order. command.text:
Implementation review requires an explicit structural revision while preserving all accepted business requirements, the public query input, at-most-ten product limit, actual document write with its output reference, and unconditional browser cleanup. Do not remove existing business work.
The proposed read/extraction composition is not ready for approval: it ignores every authoritative truncation flag, uses guessed product selectors, and uses interpret for observed product-field extraction. Compilation does not prove complete observations. Use inspected producer contracts: bounded observation manifests and existing loops must consume every listed page before navigation/click invalidates its snapshot, with requires guards rejecting captureTruncated or manifestTruncated; page delivery completeness remains tied to that manifest. A bounded targeted HTML/text read is valid only with a guard rejecting truncation and with any selector derived from an actual observation. Missing or incomplete data must not become an empty successful result. Do not assume site-specific selectors or invent product URLs.
Keep this composition simple: retain full source observations; project only necessary typed record fields for the consumer. Use explicit extract transforms for source-grounded JSON/text/HTML-to-business-field extraction, declaring only needed result fields. When independent source/target arrays align one-to-one, leave runtime item processing to extraction or select existing each explicitly when ambiguous; never send an entire raw collection into a global interpret task merely to copy or extract fields. Choose complete bounded record items, not giant page snapshots. Keep only genuine decisions/selection/synthesis as interpret on compact business observations; no duplicate raw collection inputs. Extraction cannot invent status labels or metadata: use observed values, nullable missing fields and explicit business constants outside extraction where needed. No implicit filtering, sorting or flattening in one-to-one extraction.
Preserve conditional acceptance of an actually observed authorized cookie control and a fresh complete observation afterward, actual per-product visits before extraction, document writing and cleanup. A CAPTCHA or impossible completeness remains an explicit failure/limitation. Preserve valid scope exports and references. No new permissions, caller inputs, limits, runtime mechanics or scenario-specific production rules.

Preserve the current complete-manifest loops, guards, observed conditional consent, per-product visits, actual document write/output reference and root cleanup. The current revision fixes completeness, but still misuses extraction to copy typed Browser observation records and passes whole foreach outputs into consumers. Revise only this implementation; preserve accepted business requirements and unrelated work.
For each page, use its authoritative observation.records array and deterministic value/field/object bindings (copy-only foreach where necessary), not an extract transform, to construct a consumer-specific record view. Use actual declared Browser fields and their exact types/nullability; do not invent a selector field or make optional fields required by copying. Consent needs observed control text/group/role and exact selectorHints; search selection needs observed text/group/href but no selectors; product field extraction needs observed text/group/heading context, not selectors or unrelated URLs. Keep full source records available in their producer for later actions. No filtering/truncation/flattening in copy loops: preserve every record, order, duplicates and page grouping.
Export named page views and bind each consumer directly to the foreach's declared exported port; never bind the whole foreach result envelope or add the raw page alongside its view. Keep global selection of up to ten observed product links explicit as a genuine decision over compact search views, not automatic one-to-one extraction. Product-field extraction remains extract over its compact observed business view; it must not use interpretation to invent missing values. Derive missing flags through existing predicates or preserve explicit nullable result fields; do not request technical copy mappings or synthetic indices from learned extraction. One-to-one array extraction is for independent items only.
Keep required scope exports and clean references. Do not add more LLM calls solely for field-copying or wider public inputs. All limits, approval, provenance, observed visits and workbook/cleanup oracles remain unchanged.
